topic.name: Using Integration by Parts to Calculate Integrals With Logarithms

question.explanation:
First, we write the integral as \[ \int \ln(x+1)\,\textrm{d}x = \int \ln(x+1) \cdot 1 \cdot \textrm{d}x. \]

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and $v',$ as follows:

\begin{align*} u=\ln(x+1)\quad &\Longrightarrow \quad u' = \dfrac{1}{x+1} \\[5pt] v' = 1\quad &\Longrightarrow \quad v = \int\, \textrm{d}x = {x} \end{align*}

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get \[\begin{align*} \int \ln(x+1)\, \textrm{d}x &= \int u\, v'\,\textrm{d}x \\[2pt] &= uv - \int v u'\,\textrm{d}x\\[2pt] &=\ln(x+1) \cdot x - \int x\cdot \dfrac{1}{x+1}\, \textrm{d}x\\[2pt] &= x\ln(x+1) - \int \dfrac{x}{x+1} \,\textrm{d}x. \end{align*}\]

Now, we use a substitution $x+1=u,$ thus $x=u-1$ and $\textrm{d}x=\textrm{d}u.$ Hence, \[\begin{align*} \int \ln(x+1) \,\textrm{d}x &= x\ln(x+1) - \int \dfrac{x}{x+1}\, \textrm{d}x\\[2pt] &=x\ln(x+1) -\int \dfrac{u-1}{u}\,\textrm{d}u\\[2pt] &=x\ln(x+1) -\int\, \textrm{d}u+\int \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{u}\\[2pt] &= x\ln(x+1)-u+\ln u + D\\[5pt] &=x\ln(x+1)-(x+1)+\ln(x+1) +D\\[5pt] &=x\ln(x+1)+\ln(x+1) -x+C, \end{align*}\] where $C=D-1$ is an integral constant.

example.title: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing a Single Logarithmic Factor

question.explanation:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and $v',$ as follows:

\begin{align*} u=\log_5(5x)\quad &\Longrightarrow \quad u' = \dfrac{1}{x\ln 5} \\[5pt] v' = 25x^4\quad &\Longrightarrow \quad v = \int 25x^4\, \textrm{d}x = 5x^5 \end{align*}

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get \[\begin{align*} \int 25x^4\log_5(5x)\, \textrm{d}x &= \int u v'\,\textrm{d}x \\[2pt] &= uv - \int v u'\,\textrm{d}x\\[2pt] &= \log_5(5x) \cdot\left( 5x^5\right) - \int \dfrac{5x^5}{x\ln 5} \,\textrm{d}x\\[2pt] &= 5x^5\log_5(5x) -\dfrac{1}{\ln 5}\int 5x^4 \,\textrm{d}x\\[2pt] &= 5x^5\log_5(5x)- \dfrac{1}{\ln 5} \cdot x^5+C\\[2pt] &=\dfrac{5x^5\ln(5x)}{\ln 5} -\dfrac{x^5}{\ln 5} + C\\[2pt] &=\dfrac{x^5}{\ln 5}(5\ln(5x)-1) + C, \end{align*}\] where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula $\log_5{x}=\dfrac{\ln{x}}{\ln{5}}.$

example.title: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm

question.explanation:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and $v',$ as follows:

\begin{align*} u=\ln(3x)\quad &\Longrightarrow \quad u' = \dfrac{1}{x} \\[5pt] v' = 8x^3\quad &\Longrightarrow \quad v = \int 8x^3\, \textrm{d}x = 2x^4 \end{align*}

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get \[\begin{align*} \int 8x^3\ln(3x)\, \textrm{d}x &= \int u v'\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= uv - \int v u'\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \ln(3x) \cdot\left( 2x^4\right) - \int \dfrac{2x^4}{x} \,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= 2x^4\ln(3x) -2\int x^3 \,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= 2x^4\ln(3x)- 2 \cdot \dfrac{x^4}{4}+C\\[5pt] &=2x^4\ln(3x) -\dfrac{x^4}{2} + C\\[5pt] &=x^4\left(2\ln(3x)-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + C, \end{align*}\] where $C$ is an integral constant.

example.title: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm

question.explanation:
We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and $v',$ as follows:

\begin{align*} u=\log_4(2x)\quad &\Longrightarrow \quad u' = \dfrac{1}{x\ln 4} \\[5pt] v' = \dfrac{1}{x^4}\quad &\Longrightarrow \quad v = \int \dfrac{1}{x^4} \, \textrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{3x^3} \end{align*}

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get \[\begin{align*} \int \dfrac{\log_4 (2x)}{x^4} \, \textrm{d}x &= \int u v'\,\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &= uv - \int v u'\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= \log_4(2x) \cdot \left( -\dfrac{1}{3x^3}\right) - \int \left(-\dfrac{1}{3x^3} \right)\left(\dfrac{1}{x\ln 4} \right)\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{\log_4 (2x)}{3x^3}+\dfrac{1}{3\ln 4}\int \dfrac{1}{x^4}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{\log_4 (2x)}{3x^3}+\dfrac{1}{3\ln 4}\left(-\dfrac{1}{3x^3}\right) + C\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac{\ln (2x)}{3x^3\ln 4} -\dfrac{1}{9x^3\ln 4} + C\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{3\ln(2x) + 1}{9x^3\ln 4}+C, \end{align*}\] where $C$ is an integral constant.

Note that in the above calculation we used the change of base formula $\log_4{(2x)}=\dfrac{\ln{(2x)}}{\ln{4}}.$

example.title: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Integral Containing an Arbitrary Logarithm

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
First, we write the integral as

\[ \int_{0}^{(e^2-1)/4} \ln{(4x+1)}\,\textrm{d}x = \int_{0}^{(e^2-1)/4} \ln{(4x+1)} \cdot 1 \cdot \textrm{d}x. \]

We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and $v',$ as follows:

\begin{align} u=\ln(4x+1) \quad&\Longrightarrow\quad u' = \dfrac{4}{4x+1} \\[5pt] v' = {1} \quad&\Longrightarrow\quad v = \int 1\cdot\,\mathrm{d}x = {x} \end{align}

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get \[\begin{align*} \int_{0}^{(e^2-1)/4} \ln(4x+1) \,\textrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{(e^2-1)/4} uv'{\textrm{d}x} \\[5pt] &= uv\Bigg|_{0}^{(e^2-1)/4} - \int_{0}^{(e^2-1)/4} vu'{\textrm{d}x}\\[5pt] &=\ln(4x+1)\,(x) \Bigg|_{0}^{(e^2-1)/4} - \int_{0}^{(e^2-1)/4} x \left(\dfrac{4}{4x+1}\right) \,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=\ln\left(e^2\right)\left(\dfrac{e^2-1}{4}\right) - \int_{0}^{(e^2-1)/4} \dfrac{4x}{4x+1}\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{e^2-1}{4}\cdot 2 - \int_{0}^{(e^2-1)/4} \left(1-\dfrac{1}{4x+1}\right)\,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{e^2-1}{2} - \left[x-\dfrac{1}{4}\ln(4x+1)\right]_{0}^{(e^2-1)/4}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{e^2-1}{2} - \left(\dfrac{e^2-1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{4}\ln(e^2)\right) \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{e^2-1}{2} - \left(\dfrac{e^2-1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{1}{4}\left(e^2+1\right)}. \end{align*}\]
